comparator.name: Global Management of Social Issues
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS: 60 compulsory ECTS in year 1, 60 compulsory ECTS in year 2, and year 3 with 30 compulsory ECTS plus a genuine 30-ECTS mobility window that may be exchange, internship, a minor or an approved combination. Zero-credit GROW development is excluded. The 12-ECTS Wicked Problems thesis and open mobility space remain explicit, and no content is invented for the latter.
components: History of Government and Public Institutions
Mobility Window: exchange, internship or minor
Genuine 30-ECTS mobility, internship or minor space; no elective content is invented.

core: Wicked problems and organisational approaches to complex global social challenges
Organisation, human-resource management, collaboration and project leadership across cultures
Climate change and sustainability as social and organisational challenges
International organisations, global governance, law and social policy
Interdisciplinary social research, intervention and philosophical reflection
adjacent: Multistakeholder governance and humanitarian organisational response
questions: How can organisations and institutions coordinate responses to wicked global problems?
How do law, policy and governance shape responses to migration, poverty and inequality?
How can responsible management and social entrepreneurship address climate and social challenges?

selection.assessment: The closest programme owns wicked problems, international organisations, multistakeholder and humanitarian response, project management, global human-resource management and responsible cross-cultural management. Migration and international law form a coherent legal-policy direction, while poverty, inequality, climate change and social entrepreneurship form a coherent social-impact direction. Each produces a feasible and substantively distinct curriculum exceeding the 30-ECTS floor. Three alternatives is the maximum, and every generator-eligible row is owned exactly once.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

alternatives.label: Global social challenges, governance & organisations
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum integrates organisations, governance, sociology, economics, law, psychology, leadership and research around complex international social challenges.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Global Management of Social Issues: a social-scientific programme for analysing and managing complex global problems through organisations, governance, law, economics, sociology, psychology, leadership and research.
progression: Foundations in politics, sociology, economics, law, social psychology, sustainability and research precede advanced governance, organisational psychology, negotiation, public economics, social theory, intervention design, persuasive communication and independent inquiry. All formal prerequisites and verified offerings are respected; eight level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: International policy, law & migration
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum gives sustained weight to international and European governance, constitutional and international law, migration, institutions, political economy and social justice.
alternatives.concept: An international-policy direction focused on migration, global governance, law and institutional responses to complex social issues, supported by politics, history, sociology, economics, research and social justice.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, eight courses replace organisational leadership, psychology, communication and sustainability content with additional international, constitutional and European law, institutional history, entrepreneurship and environmental justice. It exceeds the 30-ECTS floor and makes legal-institutional governance the organising direction.
progression: Introductory politics, history, sociology, economics, law and research precede constitutional, European and international law, advanced politics, institutional history, social justice and research. All formal prerequisites and verified offerings are respected; seven level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

alternatives.label: Sustainability, inequality & social entrepreneurship
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum organises global social issues around climate, sustainability, inequality, responsible enterprise and organisational transformation.
alternatives.concept: A social-impact direction examining poverty, inequality and climate change through sustainability, economics, responsible entrepreneurship, organisational leadership, circular economy, ethics and intervention-oriented research.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest and international-policy programmes, this curriculum gives sustained weight to sustainability science, circular economy, ecological innovation, social entrepreneurship, environmental governance and responsible organisational change. It differs from each by well over four courses and is organised around social and environmental transformation.
progression: Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, and business, economics, research and leadership foundations precede advanced entrepreneurship, circular-resource analysis, environmental governance, organisational psychology, market research and intervention design. All formal prerequisites and verified offerings are respected; nine level-3 courses provide advanced depth.

notes.text: Tilburg integrates organisation studies, human-resource management, sociology, international law, project management and a dedicated three-year Wicked Problems sequence, followed by a 30-ECTS mobility window and 12-ECTS thesis. UCR can build coherent global-governance, international-policy and social-impact programmes, but it does not reproduce Tilburg’s fixed practicum and intervention sequence; the mobility window remains explicit open space.
